jobs.description:
About Us

Augusta University is Georgia's innovation center for education and health care, training the next generation of innovators, leaders, and healthcare providers in classrooms and clinics on four campuses in Augusta and locations across the state. More than 12,000 students choose Augusta for educational opportunities at the center of Georgia's cybersecurity hub and experiential learning that blends arts and application, humanities, and the health sciences. Augusta is home to Georgia's only public academic health center, where groundbreaking research is creating a healthier, more prosperous Georgia, and world-class clinicians are bringing the medicine of tomorrow to patient care today. Our mission and values https://www.augusta.edu/about/mission.php make Augusta University an institution like no other.

Augusta University's distinct characteristics in education and research include real-world experiences and community engagement, as well as a culture of building community, corporate and government partnerships that address health, security, economic and societal concerns locally and across the state.

The University System of Georgia https://www.usg.edu/hr/orientation/welcome_to_the_board_of_regents_university_system_office is comprised of our 26 institutions of higher education and learning as well as the System Office. Our USG Statement of Core Values are Integrity, Excellence, Accountability, and Respect. These values serve as the foundation for all that we do as an organization, and each USG community member is responsible for demonstrating and upholding these standards. More details on the USG Statement of Core Values and Code of Conduct are available in USG Board Policy 8.2.18.1.2 and can be found online at https://www.usg.edu/policymanual/section8/C224/#p8.2.18_personnel_conduct.

Additionally, USG supports Freedom of Expression as stated in Board Policy 6.5 Freedom of Expression and Academic Freedom found online at https://www.usg.edu/policymanual/section6/C2653 .

Location

Augusta University -

Our Health Sciences Campus: 1120 15th Street, Augusta, GA 30912

Our Summerville Campus: 2500 Walton Way, Augusta, GA 30904

College/Department Information

Established in 1829, the Medical College of Georgia Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, or BMB, is an academic home to interdisciplinary translational research for disease detection, prevention, and treatment. We are delighted that you have decided to visit our department's website. Our mission also includes the education and mentoring of future researchers, physicians and physician-scientists and service to the AU and greater scientific community. The research mission is focused on inventing better diagnostics and newer targeted therapies for the benign and malignant diseases of the bladder, brain, breast, eye, gastrointestinal tract, kidney, liver, and prostate. The research areas encompass biomarkers, chemoprevention, DNA damage and repair, drug resistance, the epigenome, immunotherapy, the microbiome, molecular signaling, natural products, protein modifications and targeted therapy. Our faculties are supported by major funding agencies, and the insight gained by their work has been published in reputable peer-reviewed journals. Home to the Biochemistry and Cancer Biology Graduate Program, the BMB Department offers PhD degrees, along with a combined MD-PhD program available to medical students. The students move on to competitive careers in academia, industry, and governmental agencies. The education mission is also served by faculty participation in undergraduate and graduate medical education, as well as the Student Educational Enrichment Program (SEEP).

Job Summary

The Research Assistant will provide laboratory assistance directly to the Principal Investigator and the laboratory team, with some ability to work independently in carrying out multiple techniques, including -but not limited to- culture of established cancer and normal cell lines, primary tissue cultures, proteomics (western-blot, ELISA), DNA-RNA isolation/purification, PCR/RT-PCR, immunocytochemistry and immunohistochemistry for immune cells, cancer cells, cloning, working with biological specimens, providing assistance in mouse models. Data Collection: Participate in research data collection, analysis, maintain institutional research protocols; willingness to learn bioinformatics.

Responsibilities

The duties include but are not limited to:

TECHNICAL WORK: Perform technical work in support of on-going research projects. Participate in data collection and documentation, as well as development of new research techniques and procedures.

LABORATORY ACTIVITIES: Managing day-to-day laboratory activities including ordering, updating inventories, preparing appropriate reagents and maintaining laboratory equipment.

DATA: Analyze and present data verbally and/or in writing. Work with guidelines and protocols of research projects.

OTHER: Perform all other duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in chemistry, biology, biochemistry, cell biology, social sciences, natural sciences, life, health care, or materials science directly related to the research area to which the position is assigned and experience in a research or clinical setting.

OR

Associate's degree from an accredited college or university in chemistry, biology, biochemistry, cell biology, social sciences, natural sciences, life, health care, or materials science directly related to the research area to which the position is assigned and a minimum of three years' experience in a research or clinical area.

Preferred Qualifications

Background in Cell Biology and Biochemistry. Experience in Cancer Biology or related. Experience with cell culture and molecular biology laboratory techniques, such as DNA/RNA extraction from cells and tissues, immunoblotting, gel electrophoresis and RT-PCR. Ability to handle and work with experimental mice is highly desirable.

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

KNOWLEDGE

Proficient in Microsoft Office and other computer software/databases.

Skills

Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills.

Detail-oriented with strong prioritization and organizational skills.

Abilities

Ability to maintain confidentiality.

Ability to use sound judgment and work independently.

Shift/Salary/Benefits

Shift: Days; M-F (Work outside of the standard business hours may be required)

Pay Band: B5

Salary: $17.88/hourly

Salary to be commensurate with qualifications of the selected candidate within the established range (generally minimum-midpoint) of the position

This position is (fully/partially) funded through external sources. Continued employment is contingent upon the availability of these funds.

Recruitment Period: Until Filled

Augusta University offers a variety of benefits to full-time benefits-eligible employees and some of our half-time (or more) employees.

Benefits that may be elected could include health insurance, dental insurance, life insurance, Teachers Retirement System (or Optional Retirement Plan), as well as earned vacation time, sick leave, and 13 paid holidays.

Also, our full-time employees who have been employed with us successfully for more than 6 months can be considered for the Tuition Assistance Program. Consider applying with us today!

Conditions of Employment

All selected candidates are required to successfully pass a Background Check review prior to starting with Augusta University.

If applicable for the specific position based on the duties: the candidate will also need to have a credit check completed for Positions of Trust and or approved departmental Purchase Card usage.

Motor vehicle reports are required for positions that are required to drive an Augusta University vehicle.

For Faculty Hires: Final candidates will be required to provide proof of completed academic degree(s) as well as post-secondary coursework in the form of original transcript(s). Those candidates trained by a foreign institution will also be required to provide an educational/credential evaluation.

All employees are responsible for ensuring the confidentiality, availability, and integrity of sensitive [patient, student, employee, financial, business, etc.] information by exercising sound judgment and adhering to cybersecurity and privacy policies during their employment and beyond.

Other Information

This position is also responsible for promoting a customer-friendly environment and providing superior service to our patients, students, faculty, and employees. "Augusta University is a patient-and family-centered care institution, where employees partner every day with patients and families for success."

Augusta University is a tobacco-free environment, and the use of any tobacco products on any part of the campus, both inside and outside, is strictly prohibited.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Augusta University is proud to be an equal opportunity employer welcoming applicants from underrepresented groups, including individuals with disabilities and veterans.

new_jobs.description:
Introduction

The California Lawyers Association (CLA) is the Bar association for all California attorneys. We are a member-driven, mission-focused organization dedicated to the professional advancement of attorneys practicing in the state of California. CLA has eighteen Sections including the New Lawyers Section (NLS) that share an area of interest in law and each offers top-tier programs, award winning conferences, events, and provides access to outstanding legal resources. We continuously seek new ways to expand our offerings. Through premier educational, networking, and advocacy opportunities, our members can maintain expertise in their fields, build contacts, and uphold the legal profession and system. CLA also has several initiatives that support its mission of promoting excellence, diversity and inclusion in the legal profession and fairness in the administration of justice and the rule of law.

CLA is committed to promoting excellence, diversity, and inclusion in the legal profession and fairness in the administration of justice and the rule of law. We are dedicated to the professional advancement of attorneys from a variety of diverse backgrounds practicing in the state of California. All CLA employees must demonstrate cultural fluency by proactively managing bias and maintaining sensitivity to race, color, ethnicity, national origin, physical or mental disability, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, religion, and age of our members and the legal community.

Summary

Under general direction of the Chief Governmental Affairs Officer , the Program Manager-Committees and Projects (PM) exercises discretion and independent judgment to provide a broad range of administrative, technical and managerial services to assist the organization in accomplishing its strategic goals.

The PM works independently to manage the business of and primarily provide support to the CLA Committees including Committee meetings, programs, special projects, and other duties as assigned. Secondarily, the PM also may be asked to provide support to the California Lawyers Foundation (CLF). The PM acts as a strategic advisor to committee leaders, offering input and direction to ensure alignment with CLA’s mission and long-term goals. Serving as the operational hub for CLA’s committees, the PM ensures cross-departmental communication and maintains the continuity of programs as leadership transitions occur annually. This position is key to advancing CLA’s mission through thought leadership, operational excellence, and high-level program management. This position requires overnight, out of town travel within California.

The PM performs a wide range of functions both independently and collaboratively. In addition to these responsibilities, the PM takes on numerous managerial and supervisory duties. This includes providing high-level administrative support to the senior leadership team, preparing reports and financial data, and effectively interacting with all levels of internal management, staff, clients, and vendors.

Duties And Responsibilities

Serve as a strategic advisor to committee leaders, providing high-level guidance to ensure committee initiatives align with the organizational strategy and goals
Execute all logistics and operations for Committee activities and programs, including preparing and presenting agendas, minutes, project status reports, and administrative reports for Committees
Research, analyze, create and update materials and resources to support initiative projects including project plans, toolkits, rosters, spreadsheets, web pages, PowerPoint decks, reports, brochures, program summaries, meeting summaries and other needed resources and materials
Facilitate cross-functional collaboration, ensuring efficient communication between committees, CLA’s Staff including Marketing, the Web Team and Member Services to optimize committee output
Oversee the committee appointment process, including managing applications, tracking and organizing applicants, coordinating review sessions with committees, and communicating decisions to applicants to ensure a smooth and efficient selection process.
Manage all aspects of special projects, initiatives, campaigns, challenges, competitions, and in-person events, from concept development through execution, ensuring alignment with organizational and committee goals
Collaborate with the CLA President on the ABA House of Delegates appointments process, including updating appointment application, website updates, managing nominations, roster updates and coordinating with candidates
Serve as an organization ambassador to the Committees, ensure relevant information is fully, accurately and timely communicated to member leaders
Ensure that others on the professional team are aware of Committee decisions, events and activities that may impact them and ensure that the Committee is aware of decisions, event or activities happening in other parts of CLA
Promote CLA activities to entice new membership and increase attendance
Negotiate with outside vendors for a variety of services
Manage and ensure compliance with CLA operational policies and procedures
Respond promptly (within 24 hours) to member leaders’ questions, problem-solve issues that may arise and follow questions or issues through to resolution
Establish and maintain high-level relationships with external stakeholders, driving partnerships that enhance CLA’s educational and professional development offerings
Represent CLA at programs and other functions, coordinate Committee activities with other CLA staff and outside agencies
Coordinate the development of publicity, materials, speakers, registration and programs for CLA MCLE programs
Assume primary responsibility in the management and operation of budgetary, administrative procedures and coordination and maintenance of the Office, department, or unit workflow requirements
Prepare, recommend and manage the departmental budget, including but not limited to monthly and yearly financial analysis of cost center(s), payment of invoices, monitoring expenditures and revenue accounts
Conduct major research and analysis of data and information, reports findings and makes appropriate recommendations for solution of administrative problems
Establish and maintain relationships with outside entities and individuals regarding the operation of and/or special projects for the Office
Assist with coordinating the implementation of new programs and administrative procedures and may be responsible for their operation
Consult with Committee Chairs and staff members regarding agendas, planning logistics, programs and projects.
Support the CLA leadership team as necessary
Help support the California Lawyers Foundation as necessary
Handle organizational and administrative tasks at meetings and prepare action summaries
Perform other related duties which may not be specifically included with this description but are consistent with the general level of the the responsibilities described

Three to five years of experience organizing and managing projects/programs
Minimum two years of supervisory experience
Principles and techniques of budget preparation and management
Methods of analyzing and synthesizing the specific policies, programs, projects and procedures to which the position is assigned, as well as how each interacts with the general policies, programs, projects and procedures of CLA
Strong leadership and team management skills, with the ability to mentor staff and lead cross-functional teams.

new_jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, Architecture & Automation Deployment
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

Agilent is looking for a Senior Program Manager to lead the deployment of engineering tools, automation, and AI capabilities across our R&D organization. This role owns the full cycle from understanding what engineers actually need, to rolling out the tools and systems that meet that need, to making adoption stick. You will run internal voice-of-customer efforts with engineering teams across divisions, translate what you learn into deployment programs, and drive the systematization and execution that turns a new tool or capability into something engineers actually use day to day.

This role also runs the program management behind Agilent's cross-divisional automation initiatives, including coordination with our China Innovation Center on accelerated engineering projects. You will build and manage the program plans, governance, and reporting that keep divisional teams, the innovation hub, and the CTO office aligned as these initiatives scale.

This is a program leadership role built for someone who can move fluidly between listening to engineers, structuring a rollout plan, and running the execution discipline to deliver it. A systems engineering background is highly valued: understanding how engineering tools plug into the product development lifecycle and being able to speak credibly with engineering leads about technical workflows, will make you far more effective than program management experience alone.

Key Responsibilities

Voice of Customer and Tool Strategy

Run structured voice-of-customer efforts with engineering teams across divisions to understand where new tools, automation, or AI capabilities would have the most impact.
Synthesize findings into clear deployment priorities and business cases, partnering with engineering leadership to validate direction.
Stay current on emerging engineering tools and AI capabilities relevant to hardware and systems engineering workflows.

Architecture and AI Deployment

Own end-to-end deployment programs for architecture implementation and AI capabilities across the enterprise, from pilot through full rollout.
Drive systematization: turning a promising tool or pilot into a repeatable, well-governed capability that scales across divisions.
Partner with IT, engineering operations, and divisional leads to manage rollout logistics, training, and change management.
Track adoption and usage post-deployment, and course-correct programs that aren't landing.

Automation Program Execution

Lead program management for cross-divisional automation initiatives, including coordination with the China Innovation Center on accelerated engineering projects.
Build and run program plans, governance cadences, and status reporting that keep divisional teams, strategic marketing, and the hub aligned on scope and timing.
Manage cross-time zone program cadence with the China Innovation Center, keeping risks and dependencies visible to stakeholders.

Cross-Functional Governance and Reporting

Maintain a portfolio view across architecture and automation programs, including status, risks, resourcing, and timelines.
Partner with divisional program managers and engineering leads to resolve cross-program dependencies.
Report program health and key decisions to the CTO office and other senior stakeholders on a regular cadence.

Qualifications

10+ years of program or project management experience in a hardware/instrument R&D environment, including experience deploying tools, processes, or capabilities across engineering teams.
Systems engineering background or hands-on experience working within a systems engineering process strongly preferred.
Experience running voice-of-customer or internal stakeholder research efforts and translating findings into action.
Experience with engineering tool rollouts, digital transformation, or AI/automation adoption initiatives strongly preferred.
Experience running cross-divisional or multi-site programs, ideally including work with an offshore or globally distributed engineering team.

Required Skills And Competencies

Strong program and portfolio management fundamentals: scope, schedule, risk, and stakeholder management.
Comfort operating in a technical environment, able to hold credible conversations with engineering leads about systems-level and architecture workflows.
Skilled at running voice-of-customer processes and turning qualitative input into a structured plan.
Ability to build structure and process without slowing teams down, tuned to an engineering audience.
Strong cross-functional influence and communication, able to align divisional and hub stakeholders without direct authority.

Additional Details

This job has a full time weekly schedule. It includes the option to work remotely. Applications for this job will be accepted until at least September 22, 2026 or until the job is no longer posted.

The full-time equivalent pay range for this position is $179,931.00 - $315,300.00/yr plus eligibility for bonus, stock and benefits. Our pay ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. The Digital Accessibility Program Manager serves as the operational and subject matter backbone to the Office of Digital Accessibility’s service delivery. The ideal candidate brings both digital accessibility expertise and strong program management skills, serving as a critical bridge between technical staff and Stanford clients by translating findings, balancing competing priorities, and ensuring clients leave every engagement with clear, actionable guidance. They are equally comfortable guiding a campus web team through a remediation roadmap, reviewing an engineer's audit report for accuracy and completeness, and prioritizing and managing competing tasks with concurrent deadlines.

Manage the digital accessibility service intake pipeline by triaging incoming requests, assigning work, tracking progress, and ensuring reviews and consultations are completed on schedule.

Design and evolve the digital accessibility service delivery model, determining how core services (e.g., audit intake, remediation consultation, procurement review, training) are structured and delivered to improve client experiences.
Apply a creative mindset and bring the ability to think outside the box to create innovative service offerings.

Support clients on complex compliance requirements, including situations requiring creative or non-standard solutions.
Navigate difficult conversations with stakeholders who are resistant to or overwhelmed by accessibility requirements.

VOAC recognizes the unique needs of the older adult who needs a wheelchair ramp to stay at home safely, and the preschooler whose family needs additional resources. VOAC supports veteran’s efforts to exit homelessness as well as provides a safe place for survivors of domestic violence. Wherever VOAC goes, it combines relationship-building, volunteers and quality services to lift and support our neighbor’s efforts to become self-sufficient and reach their full potential.

The Housing Case Manager provides direct services and housing support to individuals residing in the Lakewood Navigation Center, a 103-bed congregate shelter serving both men and women. This role applies best practices including Housing Focused, Trauma-Informed Care, Harm Reduction, Motivational Interviewing, Crisis De-escalation, and Critical Time Intervention

Key responsibilities include:

Service Delivery: Conduct needs-based assessments, determine program eligibility, and provide individualized case management to support shelter stability and housing goals.
Housing Support: Assist participants in securing and maintaining housing, including determining rental amounts, recruiting, and mediating with landlords, and connecting guests to income and public benefits.
Community Engagement: Participate in outreach, collaborate with service providers and multidisciplinary teams, and attend relevant meetings and training.
Documentation & Compliance: Maintain thorough records in multiple databases as required by funders and the organization. Ensure staff and participants have access to community referrals.
Program Development: May develop specialized services based on participant needs and is expected to apply current best practices in service delivery.

: Use a personal vehicle for fieldwork, maintain consistent attendance, and uphold the Social Work Code of Ethics. Approximately 90% of participants are expected to engage in case management services.

Service Coordination: Collaborate with community providers and multidisciplinary teams to deliver tailored support services. Coordinate emergency housing and relocation as needed.
Program Implementation: Develop and monitor quality housing-focused services that promote stability and support participants with substantial barriers to housing.
Documentation & Compliance: Maintain accurate records in Service Point and HMIS, including eligibility, demographics, chronic homelessness, and disability documentation. Ensure timely data entry and reporting per grant requirements.
Community Engagement: Participate in outreach efforts and maintain relationships with external agencies. Administer Coordinated Entry Standard Assessments and ensure participant enrollment in ONEHOME.
Professional Standards: Attend training, meetings, and workshops. Provide mentorship and training on best practices. Maintain confidentiality and uphold the Social Work Code of Ethics.

This position will be posted for a minimum of 5 days

Coalition Mission

The mission of the Colorado Coalition for the Homeless is to work collaboratively toward the prevention of homelessness and the creation of lasting solutions for families, children, and individuals who are experiencing or at-risk of homelessness throughout Colorado.

The Coalition advocates for and provides a continuum of housing and a variety of services to improve the health, well-being, and stability of those it serves.

Our Philosophy of Service

We believe all people have the right to adequate housing and health care. We work to remove the barriers that restrict access to these rights. Society benefits when adequate housing and healthcare are available to everyone.

We Create Lasting Solutions To Homelessness By

Honoring the inherent dignity of those we serve, affirming their capabilities, and fostering their hope that a better life is possible;
Building strong, caring, and trauma-informed communities through the integration of housing, health care, and supportive services;
Advocating for social and racial equity, inclusion, and diversity and challenging the status quo in partnership with our workforce members and those we serve;
Achieving excellence through continuous quality assurance, innovation, and professional development;
Using resources judiciously and effectively.

Position Summary

The Case Manager I works collaboratively alongside case managers, supervisors, integrated health team members, and community-based partners across the organization to promote long term solutions for families, children, and individuals experiencing homelessness or who have formerly experienced homelessness. This role is responsible for developing and implementing care plans, coordinating services and resources, monitoring client progress, providing advocacy and support, facilitating referrals to other services, and maintaining case documentation and data collection. Client Care Management and Support Services are grounded in motivational interviewing, stages of change, strengths-based case management, housing support services, recovery focused interventions, cultural responsiveness, and trauma-informed care. This position will focus on delivering outreach services, facilitating referrals and linkages to mainstream services and housing, and providing crisis intervention.

Respond promptly to crises involving residents, providing de-escalation, support, and appropriate referrals.

Assist clients in applying for and securing benefits, such as Social Security, Medicaid, and food assistance.
Facilitate referrals to external agencies and coordinate care with other service providers as needed.
Contributes to enhancing and ensuring safety by identifying and sharing relevant information related to safety concerns, emergencies, or threats to individuals and others.

Description

A world where every child is safe, every family is strong, and hope outshines hardship. We help children heal from trauma so they can build healthy relationships, succeed in education and discover their own world of opportunities and possibilities. This happens by engaging a child in the context of their family issues. We know that, to end a cycle of abuse or trauma, we must work with children to clarify their thoughts and feelings and get a realistic view of each family member’s role in their life.

In response to this community-wide challenge, Presbyterian Children’s Homes and Services (PCHAS), now operates 12 programs in 34 locations, serving nearly 4,500 children and families each year, which provide children with permanent homes and adults with increased self-sufficiency. This is accomplished by the agency’s commitment to “The PCHAS Way” which inspires the agency to be strength-focused, family-centered, and goal driven with every client.

Benefits of serving children and families in need through PCHAS include competitive salaries, flex work schedules, paid time off, medical, dental and vision insurance options, voluntary life insurance options, paid holidays, and a very generous retirement plan (after one year of service and working 1,000 hours the agency matches an employee 200% up to a 3%.

Status:
Non-exempt

Working Conditions:
Works in a typical office setting and from employee’s home, or other community location as established by flexible work agreement, to complete paperwork, documentation, and other indirect service tasks. Meets clients in home, foster home, residential facility, hospital, or other community locations as needed; drives an automobile on a routine basis in all types of areas; must have reliable transportation. Requires sitting, standing, bending and reaching. May require lifting up to 25 pounds. Requires manual dexterity sufficient to operate standard office machines such as computers, copiers, calculators, the telephone and other office equipment. Requires normal range of hearing and vision. Must have the ability and energy to visit more than one family per day.

Position Summary:
The Foster Care Case Manager (FCCM) is responsible for safety and services to children and families in foster care. Tasks include facilitating Family Support Team meetings, development of individualized care (treatment) plans, coordination of individualized services across all settings, coordination of providers working in the home, school, and community environment and documentation of support related activities and services. The Foster Care Case Manager promotes effective utilization of support services to achieve permanency for children and families.

Essential Job Functions

Follows all contractual and agency policies, procedures, and seamless delivery of services to children and their families.
Maintains a caseload of 12 to 15 children depending on program capacity and the needs of the agency. Caseload size may be temporarily increased due to a CM’s extended absence and/or position vacancy.
Provide full case management services to children and their families in the MO foster and adoptive care system from the time of assignment until case closure or transfer.
Documents all activities and maintain data entry in FACES (state online database system) and CSWIS (consortium online database system) in a timely and accurate manner.
Has face-to-face contact with each assigned child and his/her family at least monthly (may require extensive travel based on the individual needs of the child and family). Has telephone contact with each child and family support provider regularly to review provider activities and to receive reports regarding case progress.
Evaluate and factually report the impact of services to team members and judiciary; attend all court hearings; schedule, coordinate and facilitate FST meetings within prescribed time frames.
Participates in FCCM consortium on-call schedule as EOC (employee on-call) for PCHAS on a rotating basis.

Requirements

Must possess a bachelor’s degree in social work, psychology, counseling, education, criminal justice, or a related human services field. Master’s degree preferred. Minimum of two (2) years of relevant case management experience.

Other Requirements:
Must hold a valid driver’s license, have and maintain a risk-free driving record. Must be willing to undergo initial and periodic child abuse/neglect, criminal history, sexual offender, and childcare/elder care disqualification list screenings as conducted by the Missouri Department of Health and Senior Services utilizing the Family Care Safety Registry. As requested, must submit fingerprints for review by the Missouri State Highway Patrol and Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI). Must undergo a pre-employment drug screen and a pre-employment physical with the results showing no evidence of communicable disease. Must be American Red Cross first aid and CPR certified at all times.

Christian Commitment:
Presbyterian Children’s Homes and Services is a faith-based Christian organization. Guided by Christ’s love, we empower children, young adults, and families by nurturing their strengths, resilience, and faith. We strive to serve like Jesus. We meet our clients where they are and treat them with respect. We focus on our clients’ strengths rather than their problems. And we encourage our clients to focus on their future rather than their past. When we do this well, we help our clients find hope and know the love of God.

A proud member of the Quanta Services family of companies, Ampacity, LLC (Ampacity) delivers a forward-thinking approach to structural and electrical solutions for clean energy transition projects. About This Role

Ampacity is seeking a Supply Chain Program Manager to own the end-to-end coordination of vendor-direct (drop ship) material shipments to project sites. This role acts as the central point of communication between vendors, 3PLs, project managers, and site receiving teams to ensure drop ship materials arrive on schedule, in good condition, and with minimal handling costs. The ideal candidate is highly organized, comfortable managing multiple moving schedules at once, and skilled at resolving logistics issues before they impact project timelines or month-end close .

Lead day-to-day shipping communication with vendors.
Monitor and respond to schedule changes, including daily truck volume, weather delays, and trucking issues.
Follow up on and resolve quality and allocation issues with vendors.
Identify opportunities to drop ship more material directly from vendors to site, reducing costs from double handling.
Track open inbound shipments to support accurate , on-time month-end close.

Experience in supply chain, logistics , procurement, or project coordination, ideally within construction, industrial, or capital projects environments.
Strong working knowledge of inbound logistics , freight/trucking operations, and 3PL management.
Excellent communication skills, with a track record of coordinating across vendors, carriers, project teams, and site personnel — even as schedules and conditions change.

Time off you'll actually use: vacation, sick days, holidays, parental, and bereavement leave

Wellness resources to help you show up as your best self, at work and at home

Job Summary

Discover a rewarding career at Arcare.
We are seeking a dedicated and patient-focused Chronic Disease Case Manager LPN to join the Arcare team. In this role, you will provide education and case management support to patients living with chronic diseases, including those with HIV. You will work closely with healthcare providers, care teams, and external organizations to ensure patients receive the support they need to manage their health effectively.

Responsibilities include coordinating chronic care services, providing health education, monitoring patient progress, and assisting with referrals. The ideal candidate will possess excellent communication skills, a strong understanding of chronic disease management, and the ability to build meaningful relationships with patients and their care teams. This role combines hands-on support with administrative duties to improve patient outcomes and promote overall well-being.

Key Responsibilities

Develop individualized care plans for patients enrolled in chronic disease management programs.
Monitor and update care plans regularly based on patient needs and acuity levels.
Provide health education on disease prevention, management, and healthy lifestyle habits.
Assist patients with navigating healthcare systems, including scheduling appointments and accessing resources.
Conduct regular follow-ups with patients via phone, telehealth, or in-person visits.
Collaborate with healthcare providers to coordinate care and case conferences.
Maintain accurate and timely documentation in electronic health records (EHR) and other required systems.
Advocate for patients by connecting them to community resources and support services.
Provide education about medication adherence, disease management, and risk reduction.
Participate in outreach events and community activities as directed.
Ensure compliance with all federal, state, and local regulations related to care delivery.

Strong communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work with diverse populations
Knowledge of chronic disease management and local healthcare resources
Ability to adapt to changing environments and technologies
Detail-oriented with strong organizational and time-management skills

Founded on the belief that healthcare is a right, not a privilege, Arcare exists to make comprehensive, high-quality care accessible to everyone, especially in rural and underserved communities. What began in the rural Arkansas delta has grown into a multi-state healthcare network, but our mission remains the same: Health for All

We invest in our people by supporting professional development, encouraging leadership growth, and providing opportunities to build long-term careers within the organization. A healthy work-life balance and a predictable schedule are part of our workplace culture.

Whether caring for patients in the clinic, supporting operations behind the scenes, or serving communities through outreach and education, our teams are united by a shared purpose: delivering compassionate, accessible care that improves lives.

Job Description

Are you looking for a career and not just a job in the Medical field? Virginia Cancer Specialists, affiliated with McKesson Specialty Health and US Oncology, a leader in cancer care, is seeking an experienced full time Patient Care Coordinator
for our Reston office.

SCOPE: Under direct supervision, serves as the patients medical liaison among the practice, hospital, support services, and payors. Relies on instructions and pre-established guidelines to perform the functions of the job. Learns how to appropriately apply department procedures & policies. Escalates issues to supervisor for guidance. Performs a wide variety of tasks. A certain degree of creativity and latitude is required. Supports and adheres to the US Oncology Compliance Program, to include the Code of Ethics and Business Standards.

Responsibilities

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Prior to a patients first appointment, contacts or meets with patient to obtain basic chart information (diagnosis, referring physician, personal data, insurance, etc). Asks patient questions regarding medical style in order to match with Network physician style (or bed side manner). Inquires about patients family, medical, social services needs.
On behalf of the patient, coordinates physician referrals, schedules oncology related medical appointments within and outside the practice, resolves insurance billing and coding issues, contacts agencies. Ensures accurate document is in the medical chart.
Responsible for insurance verification and eligibility, assessment of patient financial requirements, educating patients on insurance benefits and co-payments. Obtains pre-authorization of services. Obtains and maintains accurate patient demographics. May assist patients with obtaining financial resources.
Provides educational materials to patient and family. Updates, orders and maintains patient education materials including brochures, videos, and teaching materials.
Refers patient or family members to agencies and services such as housing, transportation, pharmaceutical needs, beauty supplies (wigs), prosthesis, counseling, etc. Networks within the community to learn about and maintain an agency & services resource list.
Researches and responds to routine inquiries in a timely and professional manner. Requests assistance from more senior coworkers & supervisor to resolve non-routine issues.

Qualifications

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: High School diploma or equivalent required. Some college preferred. At least two (2) years of directly related experience such as medical coding or billing, patient advocate, or social services, required. Must demonstrate the ability to verbally articulate information and questions with others in order to perform responsibilities effectively. Must be personable. Proficiency with computer systems, medical billing systems, and MicroSoft Office Outlook & Word, required.

The employee frequently is required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel and occasionally required to reach with hands and arms. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 10 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and ability to adjust focus.

WORK ENVIRONMENT: The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Work is performed in a clinical environment and requires frequent interaction with staff, patients and the public. Work may require minimal travel by automobile to other USON buildings.

Join us at Virginia Cancer Specialists, where meeting and exceeding the needs of our patients is our primary goal!

Job Description Summary

The Regional Hub Program Coordinator of Hutchinson provides operational and administrative support for the Thrive Kansas Digital Mental Health Initiative within an assigned Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) regional hub. This position coordinates day-to-day implementation activities, training and onboarding logistics, meeting and communication activities, documentation and record management, and project tracking. The role serves as a key resource for participating sites, community health workers (CHWs), providers, implementation partners, and regional leadership, helping ensure regional activities are completed efficiently, consistently, and in alignment with project timelines, reporting requirements, and continuous quality improvement (CQI) processes.

The Thrive Kansas Digital Mental Health Initiative is a grant funded, statewide, evidence-based digital therapeutic strategy designed to expand access to treatment for depression, substance use disorders (SUD) and other mental disorders in rural Kansas. The initiative deploys clinically validated computerized mental health interventions supported by community-based facilitation and integrated into rural primary care, behavioral health, and community settings.

Regional Deployment & Site Coordination

Schedule and coordinate deployment-related meetings and communications. Log, monitor, and route technical issues to appropriate project personnel and track issue resolution.

new_jobs.title: Development Coordinator - Kintsugi Village
new_jobs.description:
About Kintsugi Village

Kintsugi Village is a gathering place in Detroit designed to bring people together through learning, creativity and shared experiences. Inspired by the Japanese art of Kintsugi — repairing broken pottery with gold — the Village is rooted in the belief that connection, belonging and meaningful experiences can help people grow and transform.

We are building Kintsugi Village with an entrepreneurial spirit, a strong culture and a deeply personal approach to relationships.

The Role

We are looking for an exceptionally organized, warm and responsive Development Coordinator to support our fundraising and donor engagement efforts.

This is not primarily a frontline fundraising or grant-writing position. Our founders and senior leadership take the lead in building relationships with donors, foundations and community partners. The Development Coordinator makes sure those relationships are supported exceptionally well — that information is organized, commitments are tracked, follow-up happens quickly and every interaction reflects the warmth and hospitality of Kintsugi Village.

The right person will enjoy being the person who keeps things moving. They notice details, anticipate what needs to happen next and take pride in making sure nothing falls through the cracks.

What You'll Do

Donor Relations & Follow-Through

Coordinate timely, thoughtful follow-up with donors, prospective donors, foundations and other partners.
Track conversations, commitments, next steps and important relationship milestones.
Prepare acknowledgment letters, thank-you notes and other donor communications.
Help ensure that every donor and prospective donor receives a personal, responsive and welcoming experience.
Maintain a system for regular donor touches and help identify when relationships need attention.
Support stewardship activities throughout the year, not simply when a gift is being requested.

Development Operations

Manage and maintain the donor database, ensuring information is accurate, current and useful.
Enter gifts, contacts, notes and other relationship information promptly.
Maintain prospect lists, donor histories, contact reports and fundraising activity.
Track proposals, grants, reporting deadlines, pledges and other commitments.
Produce simple reports and dashboards that help leadership understand fundraising activity, upcoming priorities and next steps.
Help maintain an organized development calendar so deadlines and opportunities are anticipated rather than discovered at the last minute.

Leadership Support

Prepare background materials and briefing notes before donor and foundation meetings.
Help research prospective donors, foundations and partners.
Attend selected development meetings to capture notes, commitments and next steps.
Turn conversations into action by assigning and tracking follow-up immediately after meetings.
Draft correspondence, proposals and other materials as needed, working closely with leadership on content and tone.
Help leadership stay focused on relationships by handling the organization and administration behind them.

Tours, Events & Hospitality

Help coordinate donor visits, tours, small gatherings and special events.
Make sure guests feel expected and welcomed from the moment they arrive.
Coordinate invitations, RSVPs, materials and follow-up.
Work across the Kintsugi Village team to create thoughtful, personal experiences for donors and guests.

Volunteer Coordination & Management

Coordinate volunteers across all areas of Kintsugi Village, including the school, garden, arts, culinary programs, events and community experiences.
Develop and maintain simple systems for volunteer recruitment, onboarding, scheduling, communication and tracking.
Serve as the primary point of contact for volunteers, making sure they know where they are needed, what is expected and how they can contribute.
Work with program and team leaders to anticipate volunteer needs and proactively recruit and schedule support.
Welcome and orient new volunteers, helping them feel connected to the Village and confident in their role.
Create a warm, organized and meaningful volunteer experience through thoughtful communication, recognition and follow-up.
Track volunteer participation, interests and engagement and identify opportunities to deepen relationships and involve volunteers more fully in the Village.

What We're Looking For

Above all, we're looking for someone who genuinely enjoys supporting people and relationships.

The ideal candidate is:

Exceptionally organized. You create systems, keep good records and rarely let something fall through the cracks.

Highly responsive. You believe that getting back to people quickly matters and understand that responsiveness communicates respect.

A strong communicator. You write clearly, speak comfortably with people from many different backgrounds and understand the importance of tone.

Warm and hospitable. Kindness and personal connection come naturally to you.

Proactive. You don't simply wait for assignments. You anticipate what needs to happen and respectfully remind others when something needs attention.

Detail-oriented without losing sight of people. You understand that a donor database represents relationships, not just records.

Comfortable with informality. We work hard, communicate openly, laugh often and don't place much value on hierarchy or formality.

Collaborative and low-ego. You're comfortable working behind the scenes and take satisfaction in helping the entire team succeed.

Curious and eager to learn. You want to understand our work, our community and why Kintsugi Village matters.

Personally connected to the mission. We want someone who feels genuine enthusiasm for what we are building and enjoys sharing that enthusiasm with others.

Experience

We care more about the person than a particular résumé. Experience in nonprofit development, donor relations, executive support, customer/client service, hospitality, project coordination or a similar relationship-oriented role could all be relevant.

Experience with donor databases or CRM systems is helpful, as is comfort with Microsoft Office/Google Workspace and learning new technology. Strong written communication and demonstrated organizational skills are essential.

How We Work

Culture matters deeply at Kintsugi Village. We believe in responsiveness, kindness, openness, respect and treating every person with dignity. We value people who communicate directly, take ownership of their work, help one another and bring positive energy to the Village.

This role will have access to sensitive donor and organizational information, so discretion, good judgment and confidentiality are essential.

Most importantly, we want someone who sees development the way we do: as relationship building. Your role is to help us care for those relationships exceptionally well.

This position will be posted for a minimum of 5 days

Coalition Mission

The mission of the Colorado Coalition for the Homeless is to work collaboratively toward the prevention of homelessness and the creation of lasting solutions for families, children, and individuals who are experiencing or at-risk of homelessness throughout Colorado.

The Coalition advocates for and provides a continuum of housing and a variety of services to improve the health, well-being, and stability of those it serves.

Our Philosophy of Service

We believe all people have the right to adequate housing and health care. We work to remove the barriers that restrict access to these rights. Society benefits when adequate housing and healthcare are available to everyone.

We Create Lasting Solutions To Homelessness By

Honoring the inherent dignity of those we serve, affirming their capabilities, and fostering their hope that a better life is possible;
Building strong, caring, and trauma-informed communities through the integration of housing, health care, and supportive services;
Advocating for social and racial equity, inclusion, and diversity and challenging the status quo in partnership with our workforce members and those we serve;
Achieving excellence through continuous quality assurance, innovation, and professional development;
Using resources judiciously and effectively.

Position Summary

The Case Manager I works collaboratively alongside case managers, supervisors, integrated health team members, and community-based partners across the organization to promote long term solutions for families, children, and individuals experiencing homelessness or who have formerly experienced homelessness. This role is responsible for developing and implementing care plans, coordinating services and resources, monitoring client progress, providing advocacy and support, facilitating referrals to other services, and maintaining case documentation and data collection. Client Care Management and Support Services are grounded in motivational interviewing, stages of change, strengths-based case management, housing support services, recovery focused interventions, cultural responsiveness, and trauma-informed care. This position will focus on delivering outreach services, facilitating referrals and linkages to mainstream services and housing, and providing crisis intervention.

Duties/Responsibilities (Essential Functions)

Manages a caseload of clients with high-service utilization and disabilities including substance use and significant primary and behavioral health care needs.
Maintain positive and co-working relationships with community partners and health providers.
Works under direct supervision, with set department parameters. Works collaboratively within a team and supports collective problem-solving efforts.
Support clients with a wrap-around care management model to ensure consistent communication, engagement, and supports clients through crisis or disengagement.
Acts as a liaison between internal program management, client referral, and community partners.
Respond promptly to crises involving residents, providing de-escalation, support, and appropriate referrals.
Work with individuals to develop and implement crisis and safety plans tailored to their specific needs.
Mediate conflicts helping to resolve issues and maintain positive relationships.
Tracks client data, client engagement, and client outcomes. Focus on individual client outcomes.
Transports clients, as needed, using a CCH vehicle or an approved personal vehicle. CCH employees must have access to reliable vehicles outside of CCH fleet. Accompany residents to appointments, meetings, and other necessary engagements to provide support and advocacy. Outreach individuals to assess basic needs, safety, and mental health resource needs.
Builds rapport and maintains on-going professional relationships with individuals in need of services to get connected to longer-term care.
Assist clients in applying for and securing benefits, such as Social Security, Medicaid, and food assistance.
Facilitate referrals to external agencies and coordinate care with other service providers as needed.
Contributes to enhancing and ensuring safety by identifying and sharing relevant information related to safety concerns, emergencies, or threats to individuals and others.
Stays current on applicable community resource list. Provides resources to community members in appropriate situations.
Participates in community collaboration meetings to address barriers faced by clients and advance the Coalition’s efforts in supporting clients.
Attends trainings related to the position with intent to bring on-going training and educational opportunities to team.
Ensure timely & accurate recording of all clinical/non-clinical services, communications, and tasks in the EHR and other systems as required while maintaining complete up-to-date charts and any future upgrades as directed.
Performs other job duties as assigned.

Education, Licensure and Certifications

High School Diploma or GED required.
Bachelor’s degree in Psychology, Social Work, Human Services, Criminal Justice preferred
Basic Life Support Certification required within 30 days of employment.
Must have and maintain in good standing, a Colorado driver’s license within 30 days of hire (with the exception of SSHC)

Experience

1-2 years of experience working with a diverse population experiencing homelessness, substance use disorders or mental health challenges, particularly those individuals diagnosed with serious and persistent mental illness (SPMI) preferred

Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to build trusting relationships with residents.
Strong understanding of housing support services principles, trauma-informed care, and recovery focused interventions
Ability to manage a diverse caseload, prioritize tasks, and work independently while also being a team player.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite.

new_jobs.description:
Summary

This is a grant funded-temporary position with anticipated funding for one year. Continued employment beyond that time frame in this position is dependent upon grant funding availability.**

The Community Health Worker (CHW) serves as a frontline liaison between MyMichigan Health and the communities we serve. This role is responsible for conducting outreach and care coordination activities to connect patients with appropriate health care, community, and social service resources that address social determinants of health (SDOH) barriers and improve overall health outcomes. This person will be a key member of ambulatory patient-centered health teams and community collaborations and will work closely with the Community Health and Population Health teams.

Responsibilities

(50%)*
Manage Community Health work queue referrals for assigned geographies. Conduct patient outreach to address identified social determinants of health (SDOH) needs. Assist patients and families in addressing health disparities by connecting them with appropriate community resources to remove SDOH barriers.

(25%)*
Promote wellness and health equity by providing locally relevant, culturally appropriate education, resources, and support to patients and community members. Assist patients with chronic disease prevention and management.

(25%)*
Maintain current knowledge of SDOH best practices, CMS requirements, community resources, and referral processes. Utilize standardized Epic documentation workflows and templates to ensure accurate, compliant, and timely documentation of interventions, outcomes, and resource connections.

Other Duties And Responsibilities

Support care team needs in provider offices as appropriate to meet payor metrics and billing guidelines.

Establish/maintain positive relationships with community partners.

Collaborate with Community Health team if/when a need for a new community relationship(s) is identified.

Advocate for patients when needed.

All other duties as assigned.

MyMichigan Health is a technology driven organization and employees need to demonstrate competency in Microsoft Windows. All employees may be required to participate in further learner opportunities offered by MyMichigan Health.

- Community Health Worker Core Competency certification is required within 6 months of hire or transfer. Cardiovascular Health (CVH) and Diabetes Micro credential course completion within 6 months of hire or transfer.

Experience in a health system, public health sector, or community benefit organization.

Knowledge of personal computers, PC applications, MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Project.

Must be self?motivated, strong problem solver, and detail?oriented.

Effectively communicate with community members, partners and stakeholders.

Communicating health information using culturally appropriate terms and concepts.

Capability to navigate complex social/health issues.

new_jobs.title: Development Coordinator
new_jobs.description:
About Kintsugi Village

Kintsugi Village is a gathering place in Detroit designed to bring people together through learning, creativity and shared experiences. Inspired by the Japanese art of Kintsugi — repairing broken pottery with gold — the Village is rooted in the belief that connection, belonging and meaningful experiences can help people grow and transform.

We are building Kintsugi Village with an entrepreneurial spirit, a strong culture and a deeply personal approach to relationships.

The Role

We are looking for an exceptionally organized, warm and responsive Development Coordinator to support our fundraising and donor engagement efforts.

This is not primarily a frontline fundraising or grant-writing position. Our founders and senior leadership take the lead in building relationships with donors, foundations and community partners. The Development Coordinator makes sure those relationships are supported exceptionally well — that information is organized, commitments are tracked, follow-up happens quickly and every interaction reflects the warmth and hospitality of Kintsugi Village.

The right person will enjoy being the person who keeps things moving. They notice details, anticipate what needs to happen next and take pride in making sure nothing falls through the cracks.

What You'll Do

Donor Relations & Follow-Through
Coordinate timely, thoughtful follow-up with donors, prospective donors, foundations and other partners.
Track conversations, commitments, next steps and important relationship milestones.
Prepare acknowledgment letters, thank-you notes and other donor communications.
Help ensure that every donor and prospective donor receives a personal, responsive and welcoming experience.
Maintain a system for regular donor touches and help identify when relationships need attention.
Support stewardship activities throughout the year, not simply when a gift is being requested.

Development Operations
Manage and maintain the donor database, ensuring information is accurate, current and useful.
Enter gifts, contacts, notes and other relationship information promptly.
Maintain prospect lists, donor histories, contact reports and fundraising activity.
Track proposals, grants, reporting deadlines, pledges and other commitments.
Produce simple reports and dashboards that help leadership understand fundraising activity, upcoming priorities and next steps.
Help maintain an organized development calendar so deadlines and opportunities are anticipated rather than discovered at the last minute.

Leadership Support
Prepare background materials and briefing notes before donor and foundation meetings.
Help research prospective donors, foundations and partners.
Attend selected development meetings to capture notes, commitments and next steps.
Turn conversations into action by assigning and tracking follow-up immediately after meetings.
Draft correspondence, proposals and other materials as needed, working closely with leadership on content and tone.
Help leadership stay focused on relationships by handling the organization and administration behind them.

Tours, Events & Hospitality
Help coordinate donor visits, tours, small gatherings and special events.
Make sure guests feel expected and welcomed from the moment they arrive.
Coordinate invitations, RSVPs, materials and follow-up.
Work across the Kintsugi Village team to create thoughtful, personal experiences for donors and guests.

Volunteer Coordination & Management
Coordinate volunteers across all areas of Kintsugi Village, including the school, garden, arts, culinary programs, events and community experiences.
Develop and maintain simple systems for volunteer recruitment, onboarding, scheduling, communication and tracking.
Serve as the primary point of contact for volunteers, making sure they know where they are needed, what is expected and how they can contribute.
Work with program and team leaders to anticipate volunteer needs and proactively recruit and schedule support.
Welcome and orient new volunteers, helping them feel connected to the Village and confident in their role.
Create a warm, organized and meaningful volunteer experience through thoughtful communication, recognition and follow-up.
Track volunteer participation, interests and engagement and identify opportunities to deepen relationships and involve volunteers more fully in the Village.

What We're Looking For

Above all, we're looking for someone who genuinely enjoys supporting people and relationships.

The ideal candidate is:

Exceptionally organized. You create systems, keep good records and rarely let something fall through the cracks.
Highly responsive. You believe that getting back to people quickly matters and understand that responsiveness communicates respect.
A strong communicator. You write clearly, speak comfortably with people from many different backgrounds and understand the importance of tone.
Warm and hospitable. Kindness and personal connection come naturally to you.
Proactive. You don't simply wait for assignments. You anticipate what needs to happen and respectfully remind others when something needs attention.
Detail-oriented without losing sight of people. You understand that a donor database represents relationships, not just records.
Comfortable with informality. We work hard, communicate openly, laugh often and don't place much value on hierarchy or formality.
Collaborative and low-ego. You're comfortable working behind the scenes and take satisfaction in helping the entire team succeed.
Curious and eager to learn. You want to understand our work, our community and why Kintsugi Village matters.
Personally connected to the mission. We want someone who feels genuine enthusiasm for what we are building and enjoys sharing that enthusiasm with others.

Experience

We care more about the person than a particular résumé. Experience in nonprofit development, donor relations, executive support, customer/client service, hospitality, project coordination or a similar relationship-oriented role could all be relevant.

Experience with donor databases or CRM systems is helpful, as is comfort with Microsoft Office/Google Workspace and learning new technology. Strong written communication and demonstrated organizational skills are essential.

How We Work

Culture matters deeply at Kintsugi Village. We believe in responsiveness, kindness, openness, respect and treating every person with dignity. We value people who communicate directly, take ownership of their work, help one another and bring positive energy to the Village.

This role will have access to sensitive donor and organizational information, so discretion, good judgment and confidentiality are essential.

Most importantly, we want someone who sees development the way we do: as relationship building. Your role is to help us care for those relationships exceptionally well.

new_jobs.title: Research Assistant 1
new_jobs.description:
Discover Vanderbilt Health
: With eight hospitals and over 180 clinics, we are the region’s largest comprehensive academic health system. Vanderbilt Health has a long tradition of providing world-class care to the people of the Mid-South, living out our mission of moving medicine forward through preeminent programs in patient care, education and research. Here you’ll find a spirit of collaboration and a supportive community where your expertise is valued, your knowledge expanded and your uniqueness celebrated. We are committed to fostering an environment where talented, compassionate people are united in bringing the most advanced care to our neighbors throughout the region.

Organization:

Section Surgical Research

Job Summary:

Job Summary

A Research Assistant 1 position is available in the Department of Surgery at Vanderbilt University Medical Center (VUMC) to support the laboratory of Dr. Robb Flynn. Under direct supervision, this individual will support a broad portfolio of translational and clinical research spanning metabolic disease, obesity, and diabetes. The role is intentionally structured as an entry-level position on a defined path toward becoming a Clinical Study Coordinator: the successful candidate will contribute to day-to-day laboratory operations and clinical sample handling while progressively taking on clinical study organization and implementation responsibilities. Training and mentorship will be provided to develop the regulatory, coordination, and specimen-management skills required to advance within the clinical research career ladder.

Key Responsibilities – Laboratory & Specimen Support

Under supervision, conduct and record experiments and assays in support of ongoing lab activities.
Read, understand, and follow experimental protocols (may include tissue culture and specimen handling).
Perform ordering and purchasing of laboratory reagents, consumables, and supplies; maintain inventories.
Prepare reagents and perform calculations involving molarity, percent solutions, and serial dilutions.
Perform clinical sample preparation and processing (blood, serum, urine), including aliquoting, labeling, and storage.
Perform tissue sample preparation and processing, including handling of muscle biopsy and other tissue specimens for downstream analyses.
Retrieve, transport, and process clinical and tissue specimens from the operating rooms and clinical areas, maintaining chain-of-custody and biorepository logs.
Prepare, operate, troubleshoot, and maintain laboratory equipment according to manufacturer and University guidelines; ensure the lab is prepared for experiments.
Follow all University safety protocols (may include use of combustibles, toxic materials, and/or carcinogens); training in bloodborne pathogens and operating-room access procedures will be provided.
Compile, interpret, and communicate data and results; provide written documentation and preliminary progress reports.

Key Responsibilities – Clinical Study Organization (Coordinator Track)

With training and increasing independence, the Research Assistant 1 will support the organization and implementation of clinical studies, building the foundational skills of a Clinical Study Coordinator:

Support participant recruitment, screening, scheduling, and coordination of study visits.
Enter and manage study data using REDCap and the Epic/eStar research environment, with attention to accuracy, completeness, and timeliness.
Maintain source documentation and assist in resolving data queries.
Assist with maintenance and organization of regulatory binders and study documentation for internal review and for regulatory authorities and/or sponsors.
Procure equipment and supplies needed to fulfill study requirements.
